text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet rotation: Neeman to Treasury, Michael Eitan to Science.
- Treasury report says GDP will grow by only 2.5 percent in 1997 despite original forecast of 4.1 percent.
- Senior Treasury officials say Yaacov Neeman will be a professional and strong finance minister.
- Treasury forecasts freeze in standard of living, sharp economic slowdown and rapid rise in unemployment in 1997.
- Foreign Minister Levy wins significant concessions from prime minister.
- Koor Industries denies plans for demerger.
- Ariel Sharon's confidants say he is fuming and Defence Minister Mordechai will pay the price for "trick" appointment of Neeman as finance minister.
- Netanyahu satisfied everyone in cabinet reshuffle, except for Sharon.
- New cabinet appointees to be presented to parliament today.
- Neeman likely to back 600 million shekel budget cut.
